गङ्ग: Gaṅga2 f.: Name of one of the rivers of the Śākadvīpa 6. 12. 29, (26). All the rivers are described as having holy water (पुण्यजलाः) 6. 12. 29, (पुण्यो-दाः) 6. 12. 31; holy and excellent (पुण्यास् ता हि सरिद्वराः) 6. 12. 32; Gaṅgā is described as having many streams (बहुधा-गतिः) 6. 12. 29.
गङ्गाद्वार: Gaṅgādvāra nt.: Name of the place where the Gaṅgā enters the plains. A. Location: On the river Bhāgīrathī 3. 80. 12-13; the place where the Gaṅgā cleft with force the Himavant mountain is called the Gaṅgādvāra (शैलं शिखरिणां वरम् बिभेद तरसा गङ्गा गङ्गाद्वारे युधि-ष्ठिर) 3. 88. 18; on the Himavant moun-tain 9. 37. 26; the Koṭitīrtha is located at the Gaṅgādvāra 3. 82. 23. B. Description: Holy (पुण्य) 3. 80. 13; (पुण्यं तत् ख्यायते) 3. 88. 18; auspicious (शुभ) 3. 80. 13; visited by the Brahmanical sages (ब्रह्मर्षिगणसेवित) 3. 88. 18, by the divine sages (देवर्षिसेवित), and by the gods and the Gandharvas (देवगन्धर्वसेवित) 3. 80. 13; comparable with the gate of the heaven (स्वर्गद्वारेण यत् तुल्यम्) 3. 82. 23. C. Holiness: (1) One who bathes there is freed of sins and goes to heaven 13. 26. 12. (According to Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 25. 13 Gaṅgādvāra in this stanza refers to the place on the river Godāvarī on the Brahmagiri mountain: गङ्गाद्वारादयो ऽत्र ब्रह्मगिरौ गोदावर्यनुगता एव ग्राह्याः भागीरथीमाहात्म्यस्य अग्रे स्वातन्त्र्येण वर्ण्यमानत्वात्). D. Importance: Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 21, 2. E. Events: (1) Epic events: (i) Arjuna, during his exile, settled down there for some time (निवेशम् अकरोत्); during his stay the place looked very splendid with the presence of the learned, self-controlled and righteous Brāhmaṇas who offered many अग्निहोत्रस् and flower offerings between the banks (?) (कृतपुष्पोपहारेषु तीरान्तरगतेषु च) 1. 206. 6, 8-10; (ii) Since the path leading to the Śveta and the Mandara mountains was difficult, Yudhiṣṭhira suggested that Bhīma and the rest might return and wait for him at the Gaṅgādvāra 3. 141. 7; (iii) Jayadratha, humiliated by the Pāṇḍavas, went to the Gaṅgādvāra and practised austerities to satisfy Śiva 3. 256. 24; (iv) Bhīṣma once lived there and satisfied the manes, the gods and the sages by per-forming rites according to the prescription (विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा); and while he was there he saw the great seer Pulastya 3. 80. 12-15; Bhīṣma went to the Gaṅgādvāra to offer श्राद्ध to Śaṃtanu 13. 83. 11; (v) From the Kurukṣetra Dhṛtarāṣṭra, along with Gān-dhārī, Kuntī and Saṃjaya, went to the Gaṅgā-dvāra and practised austerities 15. 45. 10; (vi) Yudhiṣṭhira sent many well-versed men to the Gaṅgādvāra, where Dhṛtarāṣṭra and others were burnt by fire, and asked them to prepare there the receptacles for their bones (तत्रैव तेषां कुल्यानि गङ्गाद्वारे ऽन्वशात् तदा । कर्तव्यानीति पुरुषान् दत्तदेयान् महीपतिः) 15. 47. 14-15 (Nī. however, on Bom. Ed. 15. 39. 22: कुल्यानि अस्थीनि); (vii) Bharadvāja lived there; when he there once went to the Ganges for bath, he saw the Apsaras Ghṛtācī bathing there 1. 154. 1-2; (2) Past and mythological: (i) Newly married Agastya went there with Lopāmudrā and both practised severe austerities 3. 95. 11; (ii) Once Dakṣa decided to offer a sacrifice; all the gods proceeded to the Gaṅgādvāra to take part in the sacrifice of Dakṣa 12. 274. 18, 20; the river Sarasvatī, when invited by Brahman at the sacrifice of Dakṣa at the Gaṅgādvāra, went to the Himavant mountain 9. 37. 26.
गङ्गारण्य: Gaṅgāraṇya nt.: Name of a forest. Listed among the purifying and holy spots (पवित्राणि पुण्यान्य् आयतनानि च) in Avanti in the west 3. 87. 1, 12.
गङ्गाह्रद: Gaṅgāhrada m.: Name of various तीर्थस् on the river Gaṅgā (referred to also as Gāṅga hrada 5. 33. 26). A. Holy places for bathing: (1) Situated near the Mṛgadhūma तीर्थ; after bathing there and worshipping Śūlapāṇi Mahādeva one obtains the fruit of an Aśva-medha 3. 81. 85; (2) Near the Svastipura तीर्थ; a bath there secures heaven 3. 81. 152, 153; (3) Near the Koṭirūpa tīrtha; one who observes chastity and has a controlled mind, if he bathes there he obtains for ever the fruit of a Rājasūya and an Aśvamedha (राजसूया-श्वमेधाभ्यां फलं विन्दति शाश्वतम्) 3. 81. 171, 172; (4) Near the Utpalāvana tīrtha; one who bathes (उपस्पृश्य) there and offers water to manes for a month gets the fruit of an Aśvamedha 13. 26. 33; (also see the next Section). B. Epic event: Duryo-dhana entered the Gaṅgāhrada and lay con-cealed; the Pāṇḍavas and Vāsudeva stood on the Gaṅgāhrada and challenged Duryodhana (for a fight) 1. 1. 151; C. Simile: One who is not delighted when honoured and angered when insulted and remains unpur-turbed is compared to the Gāṅga hrada (न हृष्यत्य् आत्मसंमाने नावमानेन तप्यते । गाङ्गो ह्रद इवाक्षोभ्यो यः स पण्डित उच्यते) 5. 33. 26.
गङ्गोद्भेद: Gaṅgodbheda m.: Name of a तीर्थ। If one visits this तीर्थ and fasts there for three nights one obtains the fruit of a Vājapeya sacrifice and becomes one with Brahman (ब्रह्मभूतश् च जायते) 3. 82. 58.
गण्डकी: Gaṇḍakī f.: Name of a river, also called Gaṇḍakīyā (2. 18. 27). A. Location: A river in the east, beyond the Pañcālas and near the Videhas; Bhīma in his expedition to the east won the country around Gaṇḍakī and the Videhas 2. 26. 4; the river Gaṇḍakīyā crossed by Kṛṣṇa, Bhīma and Arjuna on their way to the Magadha; situated beyond the Kālakūṭa mountain; the three rivers Gaṇḍakīyā, Śoṇa and Sadānīrā rise from the same mountain (एकपर्वतके नद्यः) 2. 18. 26-27. B. Origin: The river was produced from the waters of all the तीर्थस् (सर्वतीर्थजलोद्-भवाम्)। C. Holiness: By visiting Gaṇḍakī one obtains the fruit of a Vājapeya and goes to the world of Sun (सूर्यलोकं च गच्छति) 3. 82. 97. D. Importance: Mentioned in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 16, 2. [See Gaṇḍasāhvayā].
गण्डसाह्वया: Gaṇḍasāhvayā f.: Name of a river, identical with the Gaṇḍakī (?). Mentioned among the rivers which are called mothers of the fire-hearths i. e. on the banks of which sacrifices were performed (एता नद्यस् तु धिष्ण्यानां मातरो या प्र-कीर्तिताः) 3. 212. 24 (for Nī. see Kapilā). [See Gaṇḍakī]
गन्धतारिक: Gandhatārika nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। By bathing there (उपस्पृश्य) and by abstaining from food for a month (एकमासं निराहारः) one obtains the power of becom-ing invisible (? अन्तर्धानफलं लभेत्) 13. 26. 29 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 25. 30: अन्तर्धानफलं गन्धर्वादिभोगम्).
गन्धर्वतीर्थ: Gandharvatīrtha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Balarāma went to the तीर्थ of the Gan-dharvas (गन्धर्वाणां … तीर्थम्) from Subhūmikā 9. 36. 10, (8); there the Gan-dharvas, Viśvāvasu and others, practised aus-terites and performed delightful dances, played on musical instruments and sang (नृत्तवादि-त्रगीतं च कुर्वन्ति सुमनोरमम्) 9. 36. 11; Haladhara (Balarāma) gave there wealth of different kinds as also goats and sheep, cows, donkeys, and camels, gold and silver to the Brāhmaṇas; he also fed them and satisfied them by giving large amounts of wealth as desired; he went from the Gan-dharvatīrtha (तस्माद् गन्धर्वतीर्थाच् च), accompanied and praised by the Brāhmaṇas, to the Gargasrotas 9. 36. 12-14.
गय: Gaya m.: Name of a mountain. Situated in the east 3. 85. 3; described as an excellent mountain (गिरिवर), holy (पुण्य) and honoured by the royal sage (Gaya) (राजर्षिसत्कृत) 3. 85. 6; it (the mountain not directly named) was honoured by the pious royal sage Gaya who knew धर्म (ततो महीधरं जग्मुर् धर्म-ज्ञेनाभिसत्कृतम् । राजर्षिणा पुण्यकृता ग-येन) 3. 93. 9. [See Gayaśiras, Gayā]

Gaya m. (pl.): Name of a country and its people. A. Location: To the east of Hāstina-pura, beyond Matsya and Malaya coun-tries (ययौ प्राचीं दिशं प्रति; ततः प्राचीं दिशं भीमो ययौ) 2. 26. 1, 7; (ततो मत्स्यान् … मलयांश् च … गयांश् चैव) 2. 27. 8. B. Description: The country was rich in cattle (पशुभूमि) and the people there were blameless (अनवद्य) 2. 27. 8. C. Epic events: (1) Bhīma in his expedition to the east before the Rājasūya conquered them 2. 27. 8; (2) Distinguished Kṣatriyas of noble birth, who came for the Rājasūya with their followers and with weapons in hand, brought wealth by hundreds (गयास् तथा । सुजातयः श्रेणिमन्तः श्रेयांसः शस्त्रपाणयः । आहार्षुः क्ष-त्रिया वित्तं शतशो ऽजातशत्रवे ॥ ) 2. 48. 15-16. D. Past event: Sarasvatī, when invited at the time of the great sacrifice of Gaya, appeared in the land of Gayas and was known there as Viśālā (गयेष्व् एव … आहूता सरस्वती ॥ विशालां तु गयेष्व् आहुर् ऋषयः) 9. 37. 19-20.
गयशिरस्: Gayaśiras nt.: Name of a lake. Situated in the east (3. 85. 3), near the Gaya mountain and the river Mahānadī 3. 85. 8; 3. 93. 10; nearby stands the banyan tree Akṣayyakaraṇa (i. e. Akṣayavaṭa) 3. 85. 8; mentioned among the holy places by visiting which those that are high-souled (महात्मानः) and have observed vows (धृतव्रताः) become auspicious (शिवाः) and, acquiring for themselves a divine form (दिव्यसंस्थानाः) and wearing divine gar-lands (दिव्यमाल्यधराः) and, endowed with holy fragrance (पुण्यगन्धाढ्याः), go to the Vimāna of the cows (ते तत्र मोदन्ति गवां विमाने) 13. 105. 46, 48, 44.
गया: Gayā f.: Name of a sacred place. A. Location: Arjuna, during the period of his exile, came across Gayā while going to the east 1. 207. 7, 5; the banyan tree Akṣayavaṭa stands near it 13. 88. 14. B. Holy, important for offering श्राद्ध: (1) By bathing (उपस्पृश्य) at Gayā one is freed of the sin of ब्रह्महत्या 13. 26. 40; (2) Just by visiting Gayā a Brahmacārī who has controlled his sense organs gets the fruit of an Aśvamedha; by living there in the dark and bright fortnights one purifies, without doubt, his lineage upto seven gene-rations (पुनात्य् आसप्तमं राजन् कुलम् नास्त्य् अत्र संशयः) 3. 82. 71, 84; (3) Mentioned among the holy places by visiting which those that are high-souled and have observed vows go to the world of the cows (गवां विमाने) 13. 105. 46 (for details see Gayaśiras); (4) One of the Gāthās, sung by the Pitṛs and recited in former times by Sanatkumāra to Bhīṣma, said that one should wish for many sons so that at least one of them would go to Gayā to offer श्राद्ध near the banyan tree Akṣayya-karaṇa (गाथाश् चाप्य् अत्र गायन्ति पितृगीता युधिष्ठिर । सनत्कुमारो भगवान् पुरा मय्य् अभ्यभाषत ॥ … एष्टव्या बहवः पुत्रा यद्य् एको ऽपि गयां व्रजेत्) 13. 88. 11. 14; 3. 82. 85; 3. 85. 7; whatever is offered for the manes there—water, roots, fruit, meat, food or whatever is mixed with honey— lasts for ever 13. 88. 15. C. Past event: Mataṅga practised austerities at Gayā by standing on one toe for a hundred years in order to get the status of a Brāhmaṇa (ब्राह्-मण्यं कामयानो ऽहम्) 13. 28. 25; 13. 30. 1. D. Importance: Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 23, 2.
गर्गस्रोतस्: Gargasrotas nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Name: Named after the old ascetic Garga (तस्य नाम्ना च तत् तीर्थं गर्ग-स्रोत इति स्मृतम्) 9. 36. 16; B. Location: On the river Sarasvatī (सरस्वत्याः शुभे तीर्थे) 9. 36. 16. C. Description: Great तीर्थ (महातीर्थ) 9. 36. 14; auspicious (शुभ) 9. 36. 16. D. Past event: At this तीर्थ, the aged and the high-souled Garga, who had purified his soul by practis-ing austerities, laid down the way to acquire the knowledge of time, the deviations of the luminous bodies and the portents, both terrible and auspicious (यत्र गर्गेण वृद्-धेन तपसा भावितात्मना । कालज्ञान-गतिश् चैव ज्योतिषां च व्यतिक्रमः ॥ उत्पाता दारुणाश् चैव शुभाश् च जन-मेजय । … विहिता वै महात्मना) 9. 36. 15-16; there the sages, who had observed vows, constantly waited upon Garga to obtain knowledge of time (उपासां चक्रिरे नित्यं कालज्ञानं प्रति) 9. 36. 17 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 9. 37. 17: कालज्ञानं प्रति काल-ज्ञानार्थम्). E. Epic event: Balarāma reached this तीर्थ from the Gandharva-tīrtha; there he distributed wealth to the sages according to the prescriptions and gave to Brāhmaṇas different kinds of food 9. 36. 18-19.
गवां: Gavāṃ tīrtham nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। One of the holy तीर्थस् on the river Gomatī 3. 93. 2; the Pāṇḍavas, having bathed there, gave as gifts cows and wealth; they satisfied gods, manes and the Brāhmaṇas at this तीर्थ 3. 93. 2-3.
गवांभवन: Gavāṃbhavana nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। By bathing at this तीर्थ a pilgrim obtains the fruit of gifting a thousand cows 3. 81. 40.
गायत्र्याः: Gāyatryāḥ sthānam nt.: Name of a sacred place. Described as famous in the three worlds (त्रैलोक्यविश्रुत); one who fasts (उपोषितः) there for three nights gets the fruit of giving a thousand cows 3. 83. 26; it is a direct testing ground for the Brāhmaṇas: if a Brāhmaṇa who is of mixed origin recites the Gāyatrī stanza there it sounds like a गाथा (a non-Vedic stanza) or a गीतिका (an ordinary song) (निदर्शनं च प्रत्यक्षम् ब्राह्मणानां नराधिप । गायत्रीं पठते यस् तु योनि-संकरजस् तथा । गाथा वा गीतिका वापि तस्य संपद्यते नृप ॥ ) 3. 83. 27 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 85. 29: निदर्शनम् उदा-हरणम्; on 3. 85. 30: यो योनिसंकरजः स चेत् तत्र गायत्रीम् पठति तस्य सम्यक् पठतो ऽपि तीर्थम(? मा)हात्म्यात् सा गायत्री गाथा स्वरनियमहीना मुखान् निःसरति । गाथिका ग्राम्यगीतवत् स्वर-वर्णविकृता । गीतिकेति पाठे ऽपि स एवार्-थः । ).
गायन्तिका: Gāyantikā f.: Name of a holy place (a cave ?) Situated in the north (on the mountain Himavant) 5. 109. 3; the gate of this cave is guarded by the excellent and the high-souled sages, called Dhāmas, who speak truth (अत्र गायन्तिकाद्वारं रक्षन्ति द्विजसत्तमाः । धामा नाम महात्मानो मुनयः सत्य-वादिनः ॥ ) 5. 109. 14; as one enters it and moves beyond this point, one gets dissolved (यथा यथा प्रविशति तस्मात् परतरं नरः । तथा तथा द्विजश्रेष्ठ प्रवि-लीयति गातव ॥ ) 5. 109. 16; no one has ever gone beyond it except Nārāyaṇa and Nara 5. 109. 17; (Nī. who reads अत्र गङ्गां महाद्वारं रक्षन्ति, on Bom. Ed. 5. 111. 16: गायन्तिकाद्वारम् इति पाठे गायन्तिका बिलविशेषः).
गिरिमुञ्ज: Girimuñja m.: Name of a mountain. Described as famous in the three worlds (त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम्); after reaching there and after paying reverence to Pitāmaha one gets the fruit of gifting a thousand cows 3. 80. 102.
गृध्रकूट: Gṛdhrakūṭa m.: Name of a mountain. When the Kṣatriyas were destroyed by Rāma Jāmadagnya one of them, Bṛhadratha, was protected on the Gṛdhrakūṭa by cow-tailed monkeys (गोलाङ्गूलैः … अभिरक्षितः) 12. 49. 73.
गृध्रवट: Gṛdhravaṭa m.: Name of a sacred place. Sacred to the god given to meditation (Śiva) (स्थानं देवस्य धीमतः); if a Brāhmaṇa approaches there Vṛṣadhvaja (Śiva) and bathes with ashes (स्नायीत भस्मना तत्र) it is as good as his having observed a vow for twelve years; and if other castes do the same (इतरेषां तु वर्णानाम्) all their sins are destroyed 3. 82. 79-80.
गोकर्ण: Gokarṇa nt., m.: Name of a sacred place (स्थानम् 3. 261. 54) and a lake (ह्रदः 3. 86. 13). A. Location: In the south (दक्षिण-स्याम्) 3. 86. 1; on the western coast (अपरा-न्तेषु) 1. 210. 1; in the middle of the ocean (very close to the ocean) (समुद्रमध्ये) 3. 83. 22. B. Description: Holy (पुण्य) 1. 32. 4; 1. 210. 1; 3. 86. 1, 13; auspicious (शिव) 3. 86. 13; famous in the three worlds (त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम्) 3. 83. 22; (विख्या-तं त्रिषु लोकेषु) 3. 86. 12; adored by all people (सर्वलोकनमस्कृत) 3. 83. 22; undisturbed (अव्यग्र) 3. 261. 54; a holy and auspicious lake having cool and ample water, difficult of access to those who have not purified their souls (शीततोयो बहुजलः पुण्यस् तात शिवश् च सः । ह्रदः परम-दुष्प्रापो मानुषैर् अकृतात्मभिः) 3. 86. 13. C. A place sacred to Śiva: Favourite place of Śūlapāṇi (Śiva) (दयितम् स्थानम् शूलपाणेः) 3. 261. 54; where Brahman and other gods, sages, Bhūtas, Yakṣas, Piśācas, Kiṃnaras, Mahoragas and many others, as also rivers, oceans and mountains wait on Umāpati (Śiva) 3. 83. 23-4; (also see sections D and F below). D. Holiness: Characterized by the presence of ascetics (गोकर्णे च तपोधनाः) 6. 7. 48; one who worships there Īśāna (Śiva) and fasts for three nights gets the fruit of performing ten Aśvamedha sacrifices and the status of a Gaṇapati (गाणपत्यं च विन्दति); by staying there for twelve nights one has his soul disciplined (कृतात्मा भवते नरः) 3. 83. 25 (also see section F below). E. Epic events: (1) During his exile Arjuna went towards Gokarṇa from where, after visiting the तीर्थस् on the western coast, he went to Prabhāsa 1. 209. 24; 1. 210. 2; (2) Arjuna, protecting the horse of the Aśvamedha sacrifice, reached Gokarṇa from where he went to Prabhāsa 14. 84. 12. F. Past and mythological events: (1) Gokarṇa was one of the sacred places where Śeṣa, abandoning his brothers and mother, practised severe austerities 1. 32. 3; (2) Catuḥ-śīrṣa Ālambāyana practised austerities at Gokarṇa for hundred years as a result of which he got a hundred sons from Śarva (Śiva) 13. 18. 5-6; (3) Out of fear from Rāma, Mārīca repaired to Gokarṇa to become an ascetic (तापस्यं समुपाश्रितम्) 3. 261. 55; (4) Rāvaṇa went to Gokarṇa to meet Mārīca 3. 261. 54; (5) Gokarṇa was one of the holy places where Śeṣa practised auste-rities.
गोदावरी: Godāvarī f.: Name of a river. A. Location: Situated in the south (दक्षिणस्याम्) 3. 86. 1-2; listed by Saṃ-jaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 13. B. Description: Holy, most holy (पुण्या) 3. 86. 2, (पुण्यतमा) 3. 118. 2; auspicious (शुभा) 3. 86. 2; (प्रशस्ता) 3. 118. 2; charming (रम्या) 3. 261. 40; having ample water (बहुजला) 3. 86. 2; having many groves on its banks (बह्वा-रामा) 3. 86. 2; visited by ascetics (तापसा-चरिता) 3. 86. 2; resorted to by Siddhas (सिद्धनिषेविता) 3. 83. 30; going to the ocean (समुद्रगा) 3. 118. 2, (सागरगा) 3. 118. 3; one of the rivers which are des-cribed as mothers of the universe and very strong (विश्वस्य मातरः सर्वाः सर्वाश् चैव महाबलाः) 6. 10. 13, 35; C. Epic event: Yudhiṣṭhira, during his pilgrimage, reached Godāvarī; he bathed there (आप्लुत्य) and satisfied the manes and gods; he gave wealth to the chiefs among the twice-born 3. 118. 2-3. D. Past events: (1) One of the rivers seen by Mārkaṇḍeya in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārāyaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 94; (2) Rāma lived on its bank while in the Daṇḍaka forest 3. 261. 40. E. Holiness: (1) By visiting Godāvarī one secures for oneself the fruit of performing a Gavāmaya and the world of Vāsuki 3. 83. 30; (2) One of the rivers which are declared to be mothers of the hearths i. e. on the banks of which sacrifices were performed (एता नद्यस् तु धिष्ण्यानां मातरो याः प्र-कीर्तिताः) 3. 212. 23; (For Nī. see Kapilā). F. Importance: (1) One of the rivers present in bodily form in the Sabhā of Varuṇa 2. 9. 20-21; (2) Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 17, 2.
गोप्रतार: Gopratāra m.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated on the river Sarayū 3. 82. 63; described as best (उत्तम) 3. 82. 63; at this तीर्थ Rāma, together with his attendants, army and draught-animals (सभृत्यबल-वाहनः) abandoned his body and went to heaven 3. 82. 63; due to the strength of the तीर्थ, as also due to the favour and resolve of Rāma (तस्य तीर्थस्य तेजसा । रामस्य च प्रसादेन व्यवसायाच् च भारत), by bathing at this तीर्थ one's soul is cleansed of all sins and is glorified in heaven 3. 82. 64-65.
गोमती: Gomatī f.: Name of a river. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 17, 13; situated in the east, it flows near the Naimiṣa forest 3. 85. 1, 3-4; 3. 93. 1; (नैमिषे गोमतीतीरे) 12. 343. 2; on its bank there was the town Nāgapura (नागाह्वयं पुरम्) 12. 343. 2; Vārāṇasī is to the south of Gomatī 13. 31. 18. B. Description: Holy (पुण्या) 3. 85. 5; (पुण्यतमा) 13. 134. 22; auspicious (शिवा) 13. 134. 22; charming (रम्या) 3. 85. 5; its sandy bank was splendid (पुलिने शुभे) 12. 345. 12; excellent river (सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा) 13. 134. 22; (सरिद्वरा) 13. 134. 14; (सरितां वरा) 13. 134. 19; containing waters of all तीर्थस् (सर्वतीर्थोदकैर् युता) 13. 134. 12; resorted to by gods and sages (देवर्षिसेविता) 3. 85. 5; flowing to the ocean (सागरगमा) 13. 134. 21; one of the rivers which are described as mothers of the universe and very strong (विश्वस्य मातरः सर्वाः सर्वाश् चैव महाबलाः) 6. 10. 35; destroying sin (धूतपापा) 6. 10. 17 (or is it the name of a different river ?). C. Holi-ness: There are holy तीर्थस् on it (3. 93. 2) like the Rāmatīrtha, the Śatasāhasrika-tīrtha and the Mārkaṇḍeyatīrtha which is on the confluence of the Gomatī and the Gaṅgā 3. 82. 66, 67, 70; one of the rivers which wait on Śiva for him to bathe in (उपस्पर्शनहेतोः) 13. 134. 12; it was the place of sacrifice for gods, and the place for cooking the sacrificial flesh by Vivas-vant (यज्ञभूमिश् च देवानां शामित्रं च विवस्वतः) 3. 85. 5 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 3. 87. 7: शामित्रं शमितुः कर्म यज्ञे पशुमारणं विवस्वतः पुत्रस्य यमस्येति शेषः). D. Epic event: The Pāṇḍavas bathed in the holy तीर्थस् on the Gomatī and gave cows and wealth as gift; there they repeatedly satis-fied gods, manes and Brāhmaṇas 3. 93. 2-3. E. Past and mythological events: (1) The Brāhmaṇa who went to see the Nāga Padma-(nābha) decided to live on the sandy bank of the Gomatī till the Nāga's return 12. 345. 12; 12. 347. 14; 12. 349. 4; (2) Divodāsa founded the city Vārāṇasī to the north of the Gaṅgā and to the south of the Gomatī 13. 31. 18, 16; (3) Rāma, after his coronation, performed, in the company of gods and sages, ten जारूथ्य horse-sacrifices without any hindrance (दशाश्व-मेधान् आजह्रे जारूथ्यान् स निरर्गलान्) 3. 275. 69 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 291. 70: जारूथ्यान् त्रिगुणदक्षिणान् इत्य् अर्जुन-मिश्रः । … जरूथं मांसम् इति शाब्दिकाः॑ तदा मांसमयान् मांसादिदानप्रधानान् पुष्टान् इत्य् अर्थः । … जरूथं स्तोत्रम् इत्य् उच्यत इति जारूथ्यान् स्तोत्रार्हान् इत्य् अर्थः); (4) Gomatī was one of the rivers whom Umā wanted to consult on the duties of women as they were expert in it before discoursing on it to Śiva 13. 134. 16, 13, 19-20. F. Occurs in a simile: Pāñcālī embraced Bhīmasena as did a creeper a big Śāla tree growing on the bank of the Gomatī 4. 16. 7.
गोमन्द: Gomanda m.: Name of a mountain. Situated in the Krauñcadvīpa, one of the Dvīpas in the north; described as big (महन्त्), having all kinds of metals (सर्व-धातुमन्त्); there dwells perpetually god Nārāyaṇa Hari who is constantly praised by the liberated ones (यत्र नित्यं निवसति … । मोक्षिभिः संस्तुतो नित्यं प्रभुर् नारा-यणो हरिः) 6. 13. 8, 7, 1.
गोरथ: Goratha m.: Name of a mountain. Situated on the outskirts of the Giri-vraja, the capital town of the Magadha; it was characterised by cattle, ample water, and shining trees (गोधनाकीर्णम् अम्बुमन्तम् शुभद्रुमम्) 2. 18. 30.
गोवर्धन: Govardhana1 m.: Name of a mountain. It was held high by Kṛṣṇa to save the cows (गवार्थे) 5. 128. 45; in the opinion of Śiśupāla the mountain which was held up by Kṛṣṇa for seven days was no bigger than an ant-hill (वल्मीकमात्र) 2. 38. 9.

Govardhana2 m.: Name of a banyan tree. Karṇa told Śalya that he remembered it being told to him since his childhood that in the Bāhlīka country the gate to the king's residence was marked by a banyan tree called Govardhana (lit. where cows are skinned) and by a cross-road called Subhāṇḍa (गोवर्-धनो नाम वटः सुभाण्डं नाम चत्वरम् । एतद् राजकुलद्वारम् आकुमारः स्मराम्य् अहम्) 8. 30. 12 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 8. 44. 8: गोवर्धनः गवां छेदन-स्थानम्).
गोविन्द: Govinda m.: Name of a mountain. Situated in the Krauñcadvīpa, one of the Dvīpas in the north, it lay beyond the mountain Maināka, and beyond the Govinda lay the mountain Nibiḍa; it is described as the best (उत्तम) 6. 13. 18-19; the exten-sion of these different mountains becomes successively double (परस् तु द्विगुणस् तेषां विष्कम्भः) 6. 13. 19.

Govinda m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the nor-thern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जन-पदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (गोविन्दा मन्दकाः) 6. 10. 42.
गोशृङ्ग: Gośṛṅga m.: Name of a mountain. Situated to the south of Indraprastha 2. 28. 1; described as the best among the mountains (पर्वतप्रवर); conquered by Sahadeva in his expedition to the south 2. 28. 5.
गौतमस्य: Gautamasya vanam nt.: Name of a forest. The forest of the Brahmarṣi Gautama (ब्रह्मर्षेर् गौतमस्य वनम्); the lake sacred to Ahalyā was in that forest 3. 82. 93.

Gautamasya āśramaḥ1 m.: An आश्रम established by Gautama. A. Location: Situated on the moun-tain Pāriyātra (पारियात्रगिरीं प्राप्य गौ-तमस्याश्रमो महान्) 12. 127. 3. B. Des-cription: Large (महन्त्) 12. 127. 3. C. Past event: (1) Gautama practised auste-rities there for sixty thousand years (उवास गौतमो यत्र कालं तद् अपि मे शृणु ॥ षष्टिं वर्षसहराणि सो ऽतप्यद् गौतमस् तपः) 12. 127. 3-4; (2) A dialogue took place between Yama and Gautama at this place (गौतमस्य च संवादं यमस्य च) 12. 127. 2, 8-10.

Gautamasya āśramaḥ2 m.: An आश्रम founded by Gautama. After receiving the two कुण्डलस् from Madayantī, the wife of Saudāsa, Uttaṅka started for the आश्रम of Gautama to give them to Ahalyā (जवेन महता प्रायाद् गौतम्स्याश्रमं प्रति) 14. 57. 17; the horse (really Jātavedas) asked Uttaṅka to blow in his anus; when he hesitated, the horse told him that he (Uttaṅka) had formerly often done it in the आश्रम of Gautama (मा जुगुप्सां कृथाः पुत्र त्वम् अत्रार्थे कथंचन । त्वयैतद् धि समा-चीर्णं गौतमस्याश्रमे तदा ॥ ) 14. 57. 40; also referred to as गौतमस्य निवेश-नम् 14. 57. 54, गुरुसद्मन् 14. 57. 53.

Gautamasya āśramaḥ3 m., āśramapadam nt.: An आश्रम of Gautama Śaradvant. Described as beautiful (रमणीय) 1. 120. 7; Devakanyā (Apsaras) Jālapadī, sent by Indra, went to the आश्रम of Gautama Śaradvant to cause obstacle in his austerities (साभिगम्याश्रम्पदम् … शरद्वतः । लोभयाम् आस गौतमम्) 1. 120. 6-7; Gautama left the आश्रम and also the Apsaras after his semen, with-out his knowledge, spilled on a cluster of शर grass (स विहायाश्रमं तं च तां चैवाप्सरसं मुनिः । जगाम) 1. 120. 12.
गौतमी: Gautamī f.: Name of a river. Listed among the sacred places by visit-ing which those that are high-souled and who have observed vows acquire divine form, wear heavenly garlands, become auspicious and endowed with holy fragrance they attain the Vimāna of the cows (गवां विमाने) 13. 105. 47-48, 44 (for citation see Kara-toyinī); listed in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 16.
गौर: Gaura m.: Name of a mountain. One of the mountains which surround the Dvīpas in the oceans to the north of the Bhāratavarṣa (सर्वतश् च महाराज पर्व-तैः परिवारिताः); Gaura was in the Madh-yamadvīpa; described as great (महन्त्) and full of red arsenic (मानःशिल) 6. 13. 3-4, 1.
गौरी: Gaurī f.: Name of a river. One of the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 24, 13; all the rivers listed here are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
गौर्याः: Gauryāḥ śikharam nt.: Name of a mountain peak. Sacred to the great goddess (Pārvatī); described as famous in the three worlds (त्रै-लोक्यविश्रुत); the Stanakuṇḍas are on this peak 3. 82. 131. [See Stanakuṇḍa]
गजपुर: Gajapura, Gajasāhvaya, Gajāhvaya, nt.: See Hāstinapura.
गिरिव्रज: Girivraja m.: Name of a city, also referred to as Bārhadrathapura (2. 22. 42). A. Location: The Capital of the Magadha country (मागधं पुरम्) 2. 18. 30; 2. 19. 2, 19; निवेशो मागधः 2. 19. 1 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 21. 1: मागधः मगधदेशसंबन्धी निवेशः विन्यासः). B. Description: Large (म-हन्त्) 2. 19. 1; shining (शुभ) 2. 19. 1; charming (स्वादु) 2. 19. 1; free from diseases (निरामय) 2. 19. 1; unassailable (अनाधृष्य) 2. 19. 13; full of cattle (पशु-मन्त्) 2. 19. 1; no dearth of water there (नित्यम् अम्बुमान्) 2. 19. 1; full of good dwellings (सुवेश्माढ्य) 2. 19. 1; thronged by people of the four classes (चातुर्वर्ण्य-जनाकुल) 2. 19. 13; full of people who were satisfied and well nourished (तुष्ट-पुष्टजनाकुल) 2. 19. 13; marked by lavish festivals (स्फीतोत्सव) 2. 19. 13; the splen-dour of its markets of eatables and garlands was excellent (भक्ष्यमाल्यापणानां … श्रियम् उत्तमाम्) 2. 19. 22; the prosperity, marked by all qualities and full of all desired objects, was thriving on its streets (स्फीतां सर्वगुणोपेतां सर्वकाम-समृद्धिनीम् ॥ … समृद्धिम् … वीथ्यां तस्याम्) 2. 19. 22-23; delightful forests of Priyāla trees, shining forests of Lodhra trees stood near the dwelling of Gau-tama in the city (see Past events) (वन-राजीस् तु पश्येमाः प्रियालानाम् मनोरमाः । लोध्राणां च शुभाः पार्थ गौतमौ-कःसमीपजाः) 2. 19. 8; the city was mar-ked by the dwelling of the snakes Arbuda, Śakravāpin, Svastika and the best dwelling of Maṇināga (अर्बुदः शक्रवापी च पन्-नगौ शत्रुतापनौ । स्वस्तिकस्यालयश् चात्र मणिनागस्य चोत्तमः) 2. 19. 9; five high-peaked, bright and solid mountains Vai-hāra, Varāha, Vṛṣabha, Ṛṣigiri, and Cai-tyaka, closed on each other as if to protect Girivraja on all sides (एते पञ्च महाशृङ्-गाः पर्वताः शीतलद्रुमाः । रक्षन्तीवाभि-संहत्य संहताङ्गा गिरिव्रजम्) 2. 19. 2-3; the tall mountain (Caityaka) was honoured by the descendants of Bṛhadratha and the people of Girivraja 2. 19. 14; in the city were placed three भेरीस् which were made out of the hide of Ṛṣabha killed by Bṛhadratha; the भेरीस्, covered with the powders of heavenly flowers, produced sounds (तं हत्वा माषनालाश् (?) च तिस्रो भेरीर् अकारयत् ॥ आनह्य चर्मणा तेन स्थापयाम् आस स्वे पुरे । यत्र ताः प्राण-दन् भेर्यो दिव्यपुष्पावचूर्णिताः) 2. 19. 15-16. C. Epic events: (1) Jarāsandha held captive kings, whom he had conquered, in the cave of a mountain in Girivraja (गिरि-व्रजे । कन्दरायां गिरीन्द्रस्य) 2. 13. 62; (2) Kṛṣṇa, Bhīma and Arjuna saw the मागध town (Girivraja) from the moun-tain Goratha (गोरथं गिरिम् आसाद्य ददृशुर् मागधं पुरम्) 2. 18. 30; when they proceeded towards the मागध town (प्रतस्थुर् मागधं पुरम्), they did not enter it through the main gate but rushed towards the summit of the lofty mountain Caityaka (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 2. 21. 15: चैत्यकं नगरसूचकम्) and broke its old huge peak, honoured (by the people) with garlands, as if thereby striking on the head of Jarāsandha whom they wanted to kill (ते ऽथ द्वारम् अना-साद्य पुरस्य गिरिम् उच्छ्रितम् । … चैत्य-कान्तं समाद्रवन् । शिरसीव जिघांसन्तो जरासन्धजिघांसवः ॥ … शृङ्गं सुम-हान्तं पुरातनम् । अर्चितं माल्यदामैश् च  … ते ऽभिहत्याभ्यपातयन्) 2. 19. 14, 17-19; then they entered the मागध town (Girivraja) 2. 19. 19; after killing Jarāsan-dha, Kṛṣṇa, with Bhīma and Arjuna, mounted the chariot of Jarāsandha and went out of Girivraja; they alighted there on even ground (समे देशे) where they were honoured by the people of Girivraja and by the kings released from their capti-vity 2. 22. 13, 26, 28-30; Sahadeva, Jarā-sandha's son, after he was consecrated by Kṛṣṇa as king of the Magadha country, en-tered again the town of Bṛhadratha (Giri-vraja) (विवेश राजा … पुनर् बार्हद्रथं पुरम्) 2. 22. 42; the release by Kṛṣṇa of kings held captive in Girivraja mentioned in the summary of the Sabhāparvan (गिरि-व्रजे निरुद्धानां राज्ञां कृष्णेन मोक्ष-णम्) 1. 2. 99; mighty Jarāsandha's death-in Girivraja due to flash of Kṛṣṇa's intelli-gence predicted by Nārāyaṇa to Nārada (जरासन्धश् च बलवान् … गिरिव्रजे । मम बुद्धिपरिस्पन्दाद् वधस् तस्य भविष्यति) 12. 326. 89; (3) Bhīma, in his expedition to the east (2. 26. 1) before the Rājasūya, marched on Girivraja and made Jarāsan-dha's son pay tribute 2. 27. 15-16; (4) while recounting Karṇa's exploits, Bhīṣma referred to his overthrowing the kings, Nagnajit and others, who came together at Girivraja 7. 4. 5. D. Past events: (1) Sage Gautama begot Kākṣīva and other sons on Śūdrā Auśīnarī (शूद्रायां गौतमो यत्र  … औशीनर्याम् अजनयत् काक्षीवादीन् सुतान् ऋषिः) 2. 19. 5; formerly kings of Aṅga, Vaṅga and other countries used to delight themselves reaching the abode of Gautama (in Girivraja) 2. 19. 7; (2) Bṛhadratha killed a bull who ate beans, and then made out of his hide three माषनाल (?) drums and installed them in his town (यत्र माषा-दम् ऋषभम् आससाद बृहद्रथः । तं हत्वा माषनालाश् च तिस्रो भेरीर् अकारयत् ॥ आनह्य चर्मणा तेन स्थापयाम् आस स्वे पुरे) 2. 19. 15-16; (3) The royal sage Dhundhumāra, instead of enjoying the boon given to him by gods, slept at Girivraja (धुन्धुमारश् च राजर्षिः … प्रीतिदायं परित्यज्य सुष्वाप स गिरिव्रजे) 13. 6. 39 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 6. 39: प्रीतिदायं देवैर् दत्तं वरम्). [See Rājagṛha]
गोकुल: Gokula nt.: Name of a settlement. A number of people following the same trade (cowherds ?), skilled in warfare, who were brought up in Gokula were done to death by Arjuna when they attacked him—this is what Saṃjaya reported to Dhṛtarāṣṭra (गोकुले नित्यसंवृद्धा युद्धे परमकोविदाः । श्रेणयो बहुसाहस्राः … ते सर्वे पार्थम् आसाद्य गता वैवस्वत-क्षयम् ॥ ) 8. 4. 38.
गर्ग: Garga1 m. (pl.): Name of a people. Mentioned by Dhṛtarāṣṭra among the exploits of Kṛṣṇa who defeated them in battle along with Vatsas and Karūṣas (वत्सगर्गकरूषांश् च … अजयद् रणे) 7. 10. 15.

Garga2 m. (pl.): A class of sages (born in the line of Garga). Mentioned along with the great sages Viśvāmitra and others (महर्षयः) who appeared to Droṇa when he started fight-ing fiercely after hearing the news of Aśva-tthāman's death; they all told him that it was time for him to lay down the weapon since the hour of his death had arrived; it did not behove Droṇa to do anything which would be more cruel than what he had already done (त एनम् अब्रुवन् सर्वे द्रोणम् … समयो निधनस्य ते ॥ न्यस्या-युधं रणे द्रोण … नातः क्रूरतरं कर्म पुनः कर्तुं त्वम् अर्हसि ॥ ) 7. 164. 88-90.
गान्धार: Gāndhāra, Gāndhāraka m. (pl.): Name of a country and its people or its warriors; warriors occasionally referred to as Gāndhāraka (7. 6. 3, 7. 70. 42, 8. 27. 80); horses of the Gāndhāra country once referred to as Gāndhāraka (9. 27. 43); the country once referred to as Gāndhāradeśa (2. 47. 8) and twice as Gāndhāraviṣaya (14. 84. 18; 14. 86. 3). A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (गान्धारा दर्शकास् तथा) 6. 10. 52; (उत्तरापथजन्मानः कीर्तयि-ष्यामि तान् अपि । यौनकाम्बोजगान्धाराः) 12. 200. 40; the Aśvamedha horse went to the Gāndhāraviṣaya from Pañcanada (ततः पञ्चनदं ययौ ॥ तस्माद् अपि स कौरव्य गान्धारविषयं हयः । विचचार) 14. 84. 17-18. B. Famous for horses: Gāndhāra horses were offered as tribute for the Rājasūya (हयान् गान्धर-देशजान्) 2. 47. 8. C. Characteristics of the people and their warriors: (1) People: Living on mountains (पार्वती-यैः … गान्धारैः) 6. 20. 8; according to Karṇa, there was no purity among Gāndhārakas (नास्ति … शौचं गान्धार-केषु च) 8. 27. 80; a Brāhmaṇa once told the Kuru assembly that among the Gāndhāras a family had only one Brāh-maṇa, the rest were imprudent who behaved as they liked (भवत्य् एकः कुले विप्रः शिष्टान्ये कामचारिणः । गान्धारा  … के ऽप्य् अचेतसः ॥ ) 8. 30. 55; accor-ding to Bhīṣma, Gāndhāras did not believe in Bhūtapati as the अध्यक्ष of the world; they were sinful; they wan-dered over the earth and lived like dogs, crows, बलस् (?) and vultures; they did not exist in the कृतयुग, but were met with since the त्रेतायुग; (निरध्यक्षांस् तु … °गान्धाराः ॥ एते पापकृतस् तात चरन्ति पृथिवीम् इमाम् । श्वकाकबल-गृध्राणां सधर्माणो नराधिप ॥ न्लिते कृतयुगे तात चरन्ति पृथिवीम् इमाम् । त्रेता-प्रभृति वर्तन्ते ते जना भरतर्षभ ॥ ) 12. 200. 38, 40-42; (2) Warriors: Great chariot-fighters (महारथ), horseriders (सादिन्), controlled (यत्त), using armours (वर्मिन्) and fighting with lances which were shaped like a claw and were polish-ed (प्रासपाणि) 7. 63. 16, (नखरप्रास-योधिन्) 12. 102. 3, (विमलप्रासयोधिन्) 7. 6. 3; they also used bows and arrows, शक्तिस् and swords (चापशक्तिशरासि) 7. 70. 42; arrogant while fighting (युद्ध-दुर्मद) 6. 86. 26; very strong (अतिबल) 8. 5. 18; very difficult to be conquered (सुदुर्जय) 8. 57. 31; (दुर्जय) 8. 5. 18. D. Epic events: (1) Kṛṣṇa once quickly overpowered Gāndhāras and released the captive king Sudarśanīya 5. 47. 69 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 5. 48. 75: सुदर्शनं नाम राजानम्); (2) Bhīṣma reminded Karṇa that he had formerly defeated Gāndhāras and made them subservient to Duryo-dhana (गान्धाराश् च जितास् त्वया … दुर्यो-धनस्य वशगाः कृताः कर्ण त्वया पुरा) 7. 4. 5-6; Karṇa had defeated Gāndhāras, very strong and difficult to win, and made them pay tribute (यो जित्वा समरे वीरश् चक्रे बलिभृतः पुरा) 8. 5. 18, 20; 8. 57. 31 (a reference to Karṇa's conquest of earth before the Vaiṣṇava sacrifice of Duryodhana ? See 3. 241. 32 and Appendix I, No. 24, pp. 1078-1080); (3) In the Sabhā of Kauravas, Śakuni and his son were protected by Gāndhāras 5. 92. 49; (4) On the first day of war, in the Kaurava व्यूह, Śakuni with his Gāndhāra warriors, living on mountains, offered protection to Duryodhana (पार्व-तीयैः सार्धं गान्धारैः पाति) 6. 20. 8; the same day, five Kekaya brothers fought with five Gāndhāra warriors with their respective armies (ससैन्यास् ते ससैन्यांश् च) 6. 43. 73; (5) On the second day, Gāndhāras and others protected Droṇa in the Mahāvyūha (6. 47. 10) of Kauravas 6. 47. 14; (6) On the third day, the large army of Gāndhāras, led by Śakuni, en-gaged Sātyaki and Abhimanyu in a battle 6. 54. 6; (7) On the fifth day, the king of Kaliṅgas (Śrutāyus) was surrounded by Gāndhāras and others 6. 67. 13; (8) On the eighth day, war-arrogant Gāndhāras desirous of heaven or victory, broke the front line of the army of Irāvant and entered it (तदनीकं भित्त्वा … बलेन महता युक्ताः स्वर्गाय विजयैषिणः । विविशुस् ते तदा हृष्टा गान्धारा युद्धदुर्-मदाः ॥ ) 6. 86. 26; (9) On the eleventh day, Śakuni with his excellent Gāndhā-raka warriors riding on horsebacks, occu-pied the extreme end (प्रपक्ष) of the right side (दक्षिन पार्श्व 7. 6. 2) of the Śakaṭavyūha (7. 6. 15) of Kauravas 7. 6. 3; (10) On the twelfth day, Gāndhāras, led by Śakuni, stood at the rear (पृष्ठ) of the Suparṇavyūha (7. 19. 4) of Kaura-vas 7. 19. 11; Arjuna bewildered (व्याकु-लांश् चक्रे) with his arrows Gāndhāra warriors led by Śakuni's sons Vṛṣaka and Acala and killed five hundred of them 7. 29. 5-6; (11) On the thirteenth day, Abhimanyu killed seventyseven Gāndhāra warriors who followed Kālakeya (Subala's son) 7. 48. 7; (12) On the fourteenth day, Jayadratha, along with Gāndhāras riding on horsebacks and holding lances in hand, left to occupy the place (fixed for him) in the Vyūha 7. 63. 16; गिरिगह्वर: Girigahvara m. (pl.): Name of a people. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Mleccha people of Bhāratavarṣa (उत्तराश् चापरे म्लेच्छा जना … ) 6. 10. 63, 5; (पल्लवा गिरिगह्वराः) 6. 10. 66.
गोपराष्ट्र: Goparāṣṭra m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (गोप-राष्ट्राः पनीतकाः) 6. 10. 42.
गोपाल: Gopāla m. (pl.): Name of a group of warriors. A. Occurrence: They are mentioned mostly along with Nārāyaṇas; they formed part of the army of the Saṃśaptakas. (7. 66. 38; 8. 37. 33; 9. 2. 36). B. Des-cription: Respected by the brave (शूर-संमत) 7. 66. 39. arrogant in battles (युद्धदुर्मद) 9. 2. 36. C. Epic Events: (1) On the twelfth day of war, encouraged by Suśarman after the fall of Sudhanvan (7. 17. 27), they, along with Nārāyaṇas, returned to the battlefield determined to fight till death (ततस् ते संन्यवर्तन्त … नारायणाश् च गोपालाः कृत्वा मृत्युं निवर्तनम्) 7. 17. 31; (2) On the fourteenth day, they were among those who tried to check the advance of Arjuna towards Jayadratha 7. 66. 38, 41; (3) On the sixteenth day, they, led by Kṛtavarman, were stationed at the left foot of the Makaravyūha of the Kauravas 8. 7. 14, 17; (4) On the seventeenth day, Gopālas and Saṃśaptakas were struck with fear when Arjuna released Aindrāstra (8. 37. 31); no one of them was then able to oppose Arjuna 8. 37. 33; (5) They were counted by Dhṛtarāṣṭra among those all of whom were killed in the war of eigh-teen days 9. 2. 36; (6) They are said to have been once defeated by Karṇa in battle (कर्णेन विजिताः पूर्वं संग्रामे) 7. 66. 39.
गोपालकच्छ: Gopālakaccha m. (sg., pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (कच्छा गोपालकच्छाश् च) 6. 10. 55; Bhīmasena in his expedition to the east before the Rājasūya (2. 23. 9; 2. 26. 1) conquered Gopālakaccha (ततो गोपाल-कच्छं च … व्यजयत् प्रभुः) 2. 27. 3.
गोवास: Govāsa, Govāsana: m. (pl.): Name of a Brāhmaṇa settlement (?) and its warriors. During the war, mentioned by Kṛṣṇa along with the Dāsamīya Kṣatriyas; the Brāhmaṇa warriors from Govāsa along with the Dāsamīya Kṣatriyas, lost their lives while fighting with Arjuna during the first seventeen days of war (गोवासदा-समीयानां … उदीर्णाश् च महासेना ब्रह्मक्षत्रस्य … । त्वां समासाद्य निधनं गताः साश्वरथद्विपाः ॥ ) 8. 51. 16-17; at the time of Rājasūya, the Govāsana Brāhmaṇas brought a tribute of three billions to please Yudhiṣṭhira but were stopped at gate; when they brought in addition shining कमण्डलुस् of gold they were permitted to enter (गोवासना ब्राह्मणाश् च दासमीयाश् च सर्वशः ॥ … त्रिखर्वं बलिम् आदाय द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः ॥ कमण्डलून् उपादाय जातरूपमयाञ् शुभान् । एवं बलिं प्रदायाथ प्रवेशं लेभिरे ततः ॥ ) 2. 47. 5-6.
ग्रामणीय: Grāmaṇīya, Grāmaṇeya: Name of a people. A. Location: They lived to the west of Khāṇḍavaprastha along the river Sindhu (निर्याय खाण्डवप्रस्थात् प्रतीचीम् अभितो दिशम्) 2. 29. 2; (सिन्धुकूलाश्रिता ये च ग्रामणेया … ) 2. 29. 8. B. Characteri-stics: Very strong (महाबल) 2. 29. 8; they were expert elephant-riders (ग्रामणी-यैः समारूधा कुशलैर् हस्तिसादिभिः) 4. 31. 3 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 4. 32. 3: ग्राम-णीयै राजकीयैः). C. Epic events: (1) Nakula defeated them in his expedition to the west before Rājasūya 2. 29. 8, 2; (2) They were in the armies of both the Trigartas and Matsyas who fought with each other 4. 31. 2.
